title: Steve Jobs talks about Pixar 2007
speaker: Steve Jobs
content:
# Steve Jobs talks about Pixar 2007

**Source**: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2WeylkkLw80

**Transcribed**: 2025-12-26 11:05

---

**[Speaker 1]**: That was the first time I met Ed, and he shared with me his dream to make the world's first computer animated film.

**[Speaker 1]**: And I in the end ended up buying into that dream both spiritually and financially.

**[Speaker 2]**: Steve Jobs took a chance and invested $10 million to launch Pixar.

**[Speaker 1]**: The stuff that Ed and his team were doing was at the very high end, and I could see that it was way beyond what anyone else was doing.

**[Speaker 1]**: It was the combination of the new medium and John really bringing a character to life that made people say, oh my God.

**[Speaker 1]**: You know, and the smart ones say, look at this potential here.

**[Speaker 1]**: We were trying to pay the bills and just buy time.

**[Speaker 1]**: And that strategy, um, really turned out not to work.

**[Speaker 1]**: There's a classic thing in business, which is the second product syndrome, if you will.

**[Speaker 1]**: And that is companies that have a really successful first product, but they don't quite understand why that product was so successful.

**[Speaker 1]**: And their ambitions grow and they get much more grandiose and their second product fails.

**[Speaker 1]**: Believe it or not, Apple was one of those companies.

**[Speaker 1]**: The Apple 2, Apple's first real product in the marketplace was incredibly successful, and the Apple 3 was a dud.

**[Speaker 1]**: And so I lived through that and I've seen a lot of companies not make it through that.

**[Speaker 1]**: My feeling was if we got through our second film, we'd make it.

**[Speaker 1]**: We decided that the only course of action was to ask John to go in right after he come off of a bug's life without any rest to go in and take over that film.

**[Speaker 1]**: Our business depends upon collaboration, and it depends upon unplanned collaboration.

**[Speaker 1]**: And so we were just too spread out and the groups were, you know, developing their own styles.

**[Speaker 1]**: We were growing into several divisions instead of one company.

**[Speaker 1]**: And so the goal was pure and simple.

**[Speaker 1]**: We want to put everybody under one roof and we want to encourage unplanned collaborations.

**[Speaker 1]**: Pixar is seen by a lot of folks as an overnight success, but if you really look closely, most overnight successes took a long time.

**[Speaker 1]**: The best scientists and engineers are just as creative as the best storytellers.
